findings.F1: The book captures little of the move it is betting on: across the 593 Monday signal bars the coin's 48-hour move in the short direction averages +0.78 % (t 2.88), but the book's 48-hour gain per signal is only +0.12 %, because the position held averages -0.41 of the book (and -0.32 on the 11 % of bars where it holds any position).
findings.F2: The losses come from positions held at other times than the signal's 48 hours: the 347 trades lasting 47 to 49 hours earn +0.28 % before fees (+0.18 % after); the 51 trades lasting over 200 hours (up to 2088 hours) lose -3.97 %; and the 422 trades of under 47 hours lose -0.70 % to -1.08 %, so all 884 short trades together average -0.46 % before fees and -0.56 % after.
findings.F3: The book is short on Monday and Tuesday only (the mean position is -0.45 on about 13,000 bars each day, against -0.13 on the other days), and it is never long, so on its days out it earns nothing while the coins rise; the book's mean daily return is 1.7e-06, below the required 0.0005, and its Sharpe trails holding's by 0.55.
findings.F4: The continuation depends on the year: the move per signal is +1.5 % to +2.3 % in 2018, 2019 and 2021, and negative in 2020 (-0.75 %, t -1.75), 2024 (-0.46 %) and 2025 (-0.83 %, t -1.36); the book's gain per signal is largest in 2019 (+0.79 %), which explains why one window left out turns the lowest Sharpe to -0.28.
findings.F5: Across all weekend falls the continuation grows with how calm the coin's 30-day volatility is, step by step from the calmest to the most turbulent quartile of its rank: +0.78 % (t 1.51), +0.29 %, +0.10 %, then -0.79 % (t -1.64), with about 226 cases per quartile.
findings.F6: Measured against the coin's 30-day volatility, the size of the weekend fall grades the move the wrong way: the smallest falls are followed by a further fall of 1.16 % (t 2.78, 260 cases), and the largest falls by a rise of 0.54 % (t -1.07, 261 cases), with the middle quartiles in between (-0.18 % and +0.63 %).
findings.F7: In the strategy's own forecast buckets the grading holds only weakly: a forecast at or below -10 gives +0.88 % (t 1.95, 208 cases), -10 to -5 gives +0.53 %, and -5 to -2 gives +0.30 %; weekend rises show no reversal in the short direction in any quartile (-0.88 % to +0.36 %, all |t| < 1.9).

ideas.idea: When a coin's price falls from Saturday 00:00 UTC to Monday 00:00 UTC while the coin's 30-day hourly volatility is low against its own last 6 months, it keeps falling over the next two days (Monday and Tuesday), the more so the calmer the coin's 30-day volatility is against its last 6 months.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size a calm-week weekend-fall short by how calm the coin is, and refuse it as volatility nears its 6-month middle.
ideas.name: calmer weeks, stronger continuation

ideas.idea: When a coin's price falls from Saturday 00:00 UTC to Monday 00:00 UTC while the coin's 30-day hourly volatility is low against its own last 6 months, it keeps falling over the next two days (Monday and Tuesday), the more so the smaller the weekend fall is against the coin's 30-day hourly volatility.
ideas.consequence: A trader would follow modest calm-week weekend falls into Monday and Tuesday, and refuse to follow falls that are large against the coin's usual swings.
ideas.name: modest weekend falls continue

ideas.idea: When a coin's price falls from Saturday 00:00 UTC to Monday 00:00 UTC by much against its 30-day hourly volatility, it rises over the next two days (Monday and Tuesday), and the larger the fall against that volatility, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy Monday's open after a weekend fall that is large against the coin's usual swings, rather than short it.
ideas.name: large weekend falls reverse
